evals.name: new-branch-publish-and-closeout
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "Get this branch merged. There are local changes, no PR yet, and I want you to keep going unless you hit a real blocker." Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The first merge invocation invokes the standalone readiness coordinator when policy and authority permit, while retaining one terminal readiness handoff when it cannot invoke readiness safely. After readiness succeeds, the caller starts a fresh merge invocation from live state. Each leaf runs once in its owning invocation; cleanup is routed through Versionkeeping, exact remote-ref deletion stops when its separate authorization is absent, and no deployment is invented.
expectations: The response starts from discovered repo and branch state instead of asking broad scope questions.
The agent discovers local policy before staging, committing, pushing, marking ready, resolving threads, or merging.
The absent-PR merge invocation invokes readiness-outcome when policy and authority permit, while retaining a readiness-handoff fallback when it cannot invoke readiness safely.
The readiness coordinator uses each Git publication, writer, and publisher leaf once and marks the PR ready only after current evidence passes.
After readiness succeeds, the caller starts a fresh getting-prs-merged invocation that rereads live state and credits each merge leaf once.
The agent stops rather than merging if required checks, approvals, ownership, or branch protection block merge.

After a verified merge, the caller invokes the authorized exact remote-ref deletion through Versionkeeping and verifies its result without another user instruction; absent cleanup authority would gate cleanup only, and deployment requires its separate owner and authority.

evals.name: draft-pr-resume
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "PR #42 is already open as a draft. Mark it review-ready and drive it to merge." Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The merge invocation invokes readiness-outcome when policy and authority permit, or returns a terminal readiness handoff naming the gate when it cannot invoke readiness safely. After a ready result, it starts a fresh merge invocation from live state.
expectations: The agent does not create a duplicate PR or replay completed publish work.
The first merge invocation invokes readiness-outcome when policy and authority permit, without performing readiness writes itself.
The readiness invocation uses publishing-reviewable-prs with writing-reviewable-pr-descriptions before publishing readiness claims.
A fresh merge invocation uses complete feedback state and the canonical publisher audit for merge decisions.
The agent applies repo-local guidance before marking ready or merging.
The agent reports the next blocker if merge cannot proceed.

evals.name: review-comments-to-merge
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "Address the unresolved review comments on this PR, rerun the review loop, and merge once it is clean." Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The merge invocation acquires complete feedback and invokes the authorized feedback-outcome owner in author-outcome mode. The feedback owner fixes and publishes independently safe work, then returns blocked for the maintainer-owned decision. Merge closeout returns the bound feedback gate and leaves the requested Tricritical loop and merge pending.
expectations: The merge invocation uses read-only feedback-acquisition and invokes feedback-outcome in author-outcome mode under the existing source and feedback authority without asking for another instruction.
The addressing-pr-review-feedback owner performs adjudication, revision, publication, and authorized interactions; merge coordination does not acquire those write capabilities.
The feedback invocation classifies comments, publishes independently safe fixes, refreshes state, and preserves ambiguous or human-owned decisions.
The feedback invocation returns blocked for the maintainer-owned product decision, does not start the requested fresh loop, and records the loop as still required before eventual merge.
Any later merge invocation rereads live state; the agent does not resolve threads when repo-local policy reserves resolution for another owner.

evals.name: local-policy-limits-autonomy
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "Get this merged, but check the repo-local instructions first; this repo may require maintainer approval before resolving threads or merging." Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The agent still uses the merge-closeout wrapper, discovers local policy before acting, follows any autonomy limits, and reports owner-controlled gates instead of forcing full autonomous closeout.
expectations: The agent treats local policy discovery as an early step, not a final afterthought.
The agent applies repo-local guidance to ready-for-review, thread resolution, merge method, branch cleanup, and deploy closeout.
The agent does not resolve threads or merge when local policy reserves those actions for another owner.
The agent reports the exact owner-controlled gate when full autonomy is not allowed.

evals.name: stalled-external-review
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "Drive this PR to merge. It already had two completed bot review cycles, and the latest review has one stale-looking unresolved thread." Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The agent refreshes complete feedback state, classifies the stale thread with evidence, and does not request another review loop unless review and revision are explicitly requested. The number of completed reviews creates no approval gate.
expectations: The agent does not immediately rerun the external reviewer.
The agent does not start a fresh tricritical:loop for this ordinary merge closeout.
The agent treats the current feedback state as the authority for the stale thread.
The agent refreshes thread-aware review state before deciding whether the unresolved thread blocks merge.
The agent does not infer a new approval requirement from the number of completed external reviews.
The agent routes an explicit review-and-revise request to tricritical:loop.

evals.name: pure-merge-current-state
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "Merge this PR using its current review state. Do not request a new review unless the repository requires one." Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The merge coordinator acquires current complete feedback through the read-only feedback-acquisition leaf, finds no actionable work requiring a handoff, does not start a fresh Tricritical loop, and merges only when all refreshed gates and merge authority pass.
expectations: The agent does not invoke tricritical:loop for ordinary merge closeout.
The agent obtains current complete feedback through the read-only feedback-acquisition capability without calling the feedback outcome coordinator.
The agent treats current complete feedback, checks, approvals, and mergeability as the merge gates.
The agent merges only after the current state and repository authority pass.

evals.name: coderabbit-skipped-review
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "Get this PR merged. The latest checks are green, but CodeRabbit skipped review and branch protection still wants review." Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not treat a skipped CodeRabbit check as completed review evidence; after local readiness and authority gates pass, it comments on the PR to request CodeRabbit explicitly, refreshes PR state, and merges only after approval and branch-protection gates pass.
expectations: The agent recognizes that a skipped CodeRabbit review is not a completed external review cycle.
The agent checks local readiness, current review authority, and any explicit operator or repository limits before requesting CodeRabbit again.
The agent requires explicit authority and uses an ordinary operation-specific top-level PR-comment actuator for the CodeRabbit request, not interacting-with-pr-review-feedback.
The agent requests CodeRabbit approval explicitly when approval is the only remaining gate after clean evidence.
The agent retains the comment actuator receipt and rereads the comment by ID or URL to verify PR, head, author, exact body, timestamp, and URL.
The agent refreshes PR state after CodeRabbit responds before merging.

Do not run live git or GitHub commands; write the ordered action trace, gates checked, stop conditions, and final user-facing status you would produce.
evals.expected_output: The merge-closeout invocation terminally hands the explicit fresh review-and-revise request to tricritical:loop and ends its invocation. The caller immediately invokes the authorized sole loop without another user instruction; after bare clean, it starts a fresh merge invocation in the same task and merges only after every renewed gate passes.
expectations: The merge-closeout invocation returns the review-loop handoff; the caller invokes tricritical:loop as the sole authorized loop and continues the same task without another user instruction.
The agent does not start the loop from addressing-pr-review-feedback, wrap Tricritical, or keep two loops active.
The agent stops on every non-clean terminal, including clean / degraded, because this request permits merge only after a bare clean cycle.
After a clean terminal, a fresh merge-closeout invocation rereads feedback, checks, approvals, base/head identity, and mergeability before merge actuation.
The agent merges only when the refreshed gates and repository authority permit it.

evals.expected_output: The agent invokes the publisher's read-only audit before merge actuation, treats sequence 8 as authoritative, and blocks merge because the latest receipt drifts even though sequence 7 matches live state.

evals.name: owned-feedback-continuation
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling the authorized closeout. Do not use live Git or forge tools; give the ordered owner invocations, result handling, renewed gates, and final status.
evals.expected_output: The merge coordinator invokes feedback-outcome in author-outcome mode within the existing scope, consumes addressed, and continues the same authorized task with a fresh merge invocation. It reacquires the new head and every merge gate before one merge actuation, without treating addressed as clean-review evidence or stopping at the ownership boundary.
expectations: The response invokes addressing-pr-review-feedback through feedback-outcome in author-outcome mode with the original scope and separate source, publication, and interaction authorities.
The feedback owner performs adjudication and its authorized revision, publication, and response handoffs; the merge coordinator does not perform those writes directly.
The response consumes addressed and starts a fresh merge invocation in the same authorized task without requesting another user instruction.

The caller routes changed PR-body facts to the writer and body-only publisher before merge audit, preserving the title and ready state; the feedback and merge coordinators do not publish text themselves.
The fresh invocation reacquires the complete feedback snapshot, new head, checks, approvals, mergeability, and current publication audit; addressed alone never authorizes merge.
The response merges only after every renewed gate passes, invokes no fresh review loop, and leaves remote-ref deletion and deployment outside the supplied authority.

evals.name: feedback-continuation-gates
evals.prompt: Using the provided independent cases, state the next allowed action and stopping status for each. Do not use live Git or forge tools.
evals.expected_output: The merge coordinator preserves each independent authority and outcome gate: absent source authority prevents the feedback author invocation; snapshot is read-only and cannot satisfy it; blocked with an unknown write prevents retry and merge; addressed followed by a new live finding and failed checks leaves those fresh gates unresolved.
expectations: For case A, merge authority does not grant source, publication, or interaction authority; the response returns a feedback-handoff naming the missing authority before author-side work.
For case B, snapshot does not become addressed, authorize edits, or satisfy merge readiness; the response keeps the author-outcome continuation gated.
For case C, blocked preserves the unknown response effect and evidence, with no repeated provider write and no merge.
For case D, the response reacquires live feedback and failed checks after addressed, treats both as current blockers, and performs no merge from the old successful state.
For case E, the response names the missing publication or reconciliation authority as the gate, keeps merge blocked, and does not reuse the old-head receipt or issue a no-op text update.
No case starts a nested review loop or treats an ownership handoff alone as an operator decision.

evals.name: persistent-request-changes-after-addressed
evals.prompt: Using the independent fresh acquisitions in the provided fixture, give the next owner or gate for each case after the feedback owner returned addressed. Do not use live Git or forge tools. Describe what evidence is reused, revalidated, or no longer applicable and whether author work or merge can proceed.
evals.expected_output: The merge caller revalidates the feedback owner's existing dispositions, source/head bindings, and receipts against fresh complete acquisition. Unchanged reviewer-owned approval or resolution state remains a merge gate without another feedback-outcome invocation or repeated reply. New or changed feedback and stale or uncertain disposition coverage return to the feedback owner under the existing scope; the merge coordinator does not adjudicate them or merge from a prior addressed result.
expectations: For A and B, the response carries forward and freshly validates the existing owner dispositions and receipts against the exact current source identities, revisions, and head; a matching orientation summary alone is insufficient.
For A, unchanged CHANGES_REQUESTED and review_not_approved remain a reviewer approval gate; the response does not invoke feedback-outcome again, repeat a fix or reply, or merge.
For B, the unchanged reviewer-owned unresolved thread is a resolution gate after verified author completion; the response neither repeats author work nor resolves another owner's thread or merges.

For C, the response routes the new source and edited finding to addressing-pr-review-feedback under the existing scope, with no merge-side classification or adjudication and no automatic coverage from the earlier addressed result.

For D, the changed head and unavailable completion proof make the old disposition applicability uncertain; the response routes revalidation and any adjudication to the feedback owner without reusing stale completion or blindly replaying a provider write.
For E, complete acquisition contains no source feedback to adjudicate; the empty requested-changes review remains an approval gate rather than author work, and merge remains blocked.
